matters:
The Nasdaq led Wednesday’s rally, up 1.05%, on renewed AI-spending confidence, with IBM, Nvidia, Goldman Sachs and Caterpillar leading the Dow, per BBN Times (21 Oct). The Dow closed at its highest in about a month.

Netflix fell about 5% after a full-year revenue forecast below analysts’ expectations and a cut to ad revenue guidance; Q3 revenue was $12.87B, +12% y/y, per CNBC (21 Oct).

Meta and Tesla reported after the close on Wednesday; their post-earnings moves were not found with a dated source and are not carried.

scorecard.text: The prior regime call, tentative stabilisation, held on Wednesday: the S&P 500 rose a further 0.58% to 7,757.17, per CNN Markets (21 Oct).

The prior invalidation watch was set at Thursday’s 7,744.81 close as the level to reclaim; the S&P 500 closed above it at 7,757.17, so that level no longer constrains the index. The prior secondOrder framing of an industrial rotation also did not persist: the Nasdaq led with +1.05%.
The prior Nasdaq floor held: the Nasdaq did not slip below Monday’s 26,430.89 and closed at 26,702.86.
The prior note that Netflix’s guidance was a negative held: it fell about 5% on Wednesday, per CNBC (21 Oct).
Whether yields kept falling after the PPI print still cannot be graded: no sourced yield levels were found.
The 27-28 October FOMC has not occurred.
